description: Make Slack DMs a continuous, controllable conversation: route normal messages as follow-ups into a current AgentSession per DM conversation, add explicit New task switching (without canceling prior work), annotate late replies with work identity, and enable cancel/stop from the DM reusing existing Turn control — all by wiring the existing follow-up and Turn-control machinery into the Slack ingress path for agent-connection sessions.

tasks.title: DM current-session mapping and follow-up routing
tasks.description: Add the DM current-session mapping store (SlackDmSessionMappingStore + SlackDmSessionMappingRow, SQLite-backed, keyed by (ConnectionId, DmConversationId), implementing ISlackConnectionProviderCleanup) and replace the ingress handler's unconditional LaunchConnectionAsync call with a routing decision: after inbox dedup, read the mapping; if a current session exists, call IAgentSessionGrain.AcceptFollowupAsync directly with the Slack-derived idempotency key (slack:{team}:{conv}:{ts}) and DispatchNextAsync, then craft a follow-up-aware ack (continuing / accepted-pending / already-accepted); otherwise launch as today and upsert the mapping. Also make agent-connection a first-class source: ResolveCanonicalFollowupTargetAsync and ResolveCancelTargetAsync accept agent-connection, and QueryRowsByLabels supports ConnectionId/SlackUserId/SlackConversationId label lookups.
acceptanceCriteria: A SlackDmSessionMappingStore with GetCurrentSessionIdAsync/SetCurrentSessionIdAsync persists the current AgentSession per (ConnectionId, DmConversationId) and cascades on Connection deletion via ISlackConnectionProviderCleanup; the EF migration applies cleanly on top of the current schema.

The first DM (no current session) launches a new AgentJob+Session and records it as current; a subsequent normal DM continues that session as a follow-up input via AcceptFollowupAsync and creates no new AgentJob or AgentSession.

A normal DM sent while the current Turn is executing is accepted into a queued Turn; the Bot replies that the input is accepted and pending, not executing; the queued input dispatches after the current Turn terminates.
A normal DM sent after the current Turn has terminated still continues the same session as a follow-up, starting the next AgentTurn.
A redelivered Slack message resolves to the same SessionInput and creates no second input or Turn — both via the inbox dedup (first layer) and the AcceptFollowupAsync idempotency key (second layer).

ResolveCanonicalFollowupTargetAsync and ResolveCancelTargetAsync accept agent-connection source sessions; QueryRowsByLabels returns sessions matching ConnectionId/SlackUserId/SlackConversationId labels.

Server spec tests cover follow-up continuation, accept-and-queue during Turn execution, post-terminal continuation, redelivery idempotency, resolver acceptance, and label queries — using fake Slack ingress, fake storage, and injectable TimeProvider with no real network; npm test passes.
tasks.output: SlackDmSessionMappingStore + row + EF migration + ingress routing decision (follow-up vs launch) + AcceptFollowupAsync grain call from ingress + follow-up-aware ack text + resolver/query acceptance of agent-connection source.
tasks.notes: Implements design D1 + D2 (follow-up branch) + D4 + D5. The mapping store mirrors the SlackProviderInboxStore pattern (scoped, keyed by ConnectionId, outside Agent/Session domain). The ingress handler calls the session grain directly (it has the sessionId from the mapping) — no detour through AgentSessionFollowupRoutes. The idempotency key format matches the launch path (AgentLauncher.cs:203) so both layers of dedup use the same identity. The resolver changes (D5) are not required by the DM path itself but close the second-class-source gap for Web/CLI consistency.

tasks.title: New task switching
tasks.description: Add New task detection to the ingress handler: when the DM text starts with a recognized leading marker (e.g., 'new task'), strip the marker and route to LaunchConnectionAsync (creating a new AgentJob+Session), then upsert the mapping so the new session becomes current. The prior session's work continues independently — no cancel or stop is issued. If the stripped text is empty, reply with the existing empty-prompt rejection. The ack distinguishes 'Starting a new task' from the normal follow-up ack.
acceptanceCriteria: An explicit New task DM (leading marker detected) creates a new AgentJob+AgentSession and switches the DM conversation's current session to the new one; the prior session is no longer current.
A New task issued while prior work is executing does not cancel or stop the prior work; the prior work continues to its natural terminal result.
The leading marker is matched case-insensitively as a standalone leading token (not a substring); a normal message that happens to contain the words is not misread as New task.
If the New task marker is followed by empty text, the Bot replies with the existing empty-prompt rejection and no work is created.
Server spec tests cover New task switching, prior-work continuation, marker disambiguation, and empty-text rejection using fake Slack ingress; npm test passes.
tasks.output: New task keyword detection + launch-and-switch routing + mapping upsert + distinct ack text.
tasks.notes: Implements design D2 (New task branch) + D3. The marker is an explicit Owner action, not auto-detection (the non-goal '自动判断用户是在补充还是在换话题' excludes guessing). Slash commands (/new) and buttons are viable follow-ups if user feedback shows the keyword is insufficient (design D3 alternatives).

tasks.title: Terminal delivery work identity
tasks.description: Extend AgentJobLineage.BuildTerminalDeliveryEnvelope to include a short work label (first ~80 chars of the session's launch prompt) in the delivery payload. Extend the SlackTerminalDelivery record to declare this field and update SlackTerminalDeliveryHandler.Render to prefix the reply with 'Task: {label}' so the Owner can distinguish which task a result belongs to. The annotation is always present, not conditional on session currency.
acceptanceCriteria: Every terminal delivery reply to a DM conversation includes a concise work identity label (the original prompt's first ~80 chars) prefixed before the conclusion/evidence/next-step.
When prior work completes after a New task switch, its late reply carries the prior work's identity and is not presented as a result of the current session.
A late failure reply also carries the originating work's identity and is distinguishable from the current session's output.
The work label is derived from the session's first SessionInput and carried through the terminal delivery event to the rendered Slack reply.
Server spec tests cover work-identity annotation, late-reply distinguishability after a switch, and truncation behavior using fake Slack delivery; npm test passes.
tasks.output: Extended BuildTerminalDeliveryEnvelope (work label) + SlackTerminalDelivery record field + Render prefix.
tasks.notes: Implements design D7. The annotation is always on (not conditional on mapping state) to avoid a store-read race in the delivery handler. The JobKey is available in the event payload for unambiguous lookup if the label is ambiguous. Independent of T-001/T-002 — a pure rendering change.

tasks.title: Cancel and stop from DM
tasks.description: Add cancel/stop keyword detection to the ingress handler: when the DM text starts with 'cancel' or 'stop', resolve the current session from the mapping, find its active Turn (most recent non-terminal Turn) via ResolveTurnControl, and apply the operation using existing Turn control — cancel for a queued Turn (CancelQueuedTurnAsync, or IAgentJobGrain.CancelAsync for a launch Turn), stop for an executing Turn (ClaimTurnStopAsync + CancelAgentSession dispatch to Runner). If all Turns are terminal, reply 'that work has already ended'. Cancel against an executing Turn redirects to stop. Reply in the DM with the outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: The Owner can cancel a queued Turn from the DM; the queued Turn is cancelled and the Bot reports the cancellation.
The Owner can request a stop of an executing Turn from the DM; a runtime stop request is issued and the Bot reports the stop outcome (stopped/stop-requested/unknown).
Cancel against an executing Turn indicates that the Turn is running and a stop is required rather than performing a deterministic cancel.

A cancel or stop targeting a Turn that has already reached a terminal state reports 'work has already ended' and does not affect any Turn that started after the target — including a Turn executing under a later session after a New task switch.
If the current session has no active (non-terminal) Turn, the Bot replies that there is no active work to cancel or stop.
Cancel and stop affect only the single identified Turn; no other Turn in any session is affected.

Server spec tests cover cancel queued, stop executing, redirect cancel-to-stop, stale-entry protection, and no-active-work — using fake Slack ingress, fake Runner stop dispatch, and injectable TimeProvider for Turn-terminal timing; npm test passes.
tasks.output: Cancel/stop keyword detection + implicit current-Turn resolution + Turn control application + outcome reply in the ingress handler.
tasks.notes: Implements design D6. Reuses the Turn control logic built in issue 522 (CancelQueuedTurn, ClaimTurnStop, ClassifyTurn, stale-entry protection) — no new control path. Authorization is inherent: DMs are Owner-only (issue 514). The Owner does not need to know Turn IDs; the current work is the implied target. Slash commands (/cancel /stop) are viable follow-ups (design D6 alternative).
